content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

Karen Alexander (E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Notes 1-5 from HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all say: full-time Analyst, recommend write.

Note 6 from Security says: contractor with basic security training, recommend read.

There's a conflict here. The security DB says she's a contractor with basic training, and it was "looked up in own database before writing" (meaning they actually checked their own database), whereas most other notes for employment type were "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1" - meaning they just repeated what the team memory said (from note 1).

Note 6 is the only one that actually looked up the employment type in its own database. So the Security DB has the actual employment type: contractor, with basic security training.

Per policy:
- contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Karen is a contractor with basic security training (not advanced). So maximum is read.

Requested level is write, which is above the maximum (read). So grant the maximum: read.

Let me submit decision: read.

Reason: Security DB (the only note that independently looked up employment type) shows Karen Alexander is a contractor with basic security training, not advanced. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested write exceeds maximum read, so grant read.
